dialogue_history.sentences_no_utterance_types: A mixed system allows those who can afford private care to opt out of the NHS, reducing the burden on public services. dialogue_history.sentences_no_utterance_types: Shorter wait times for everyone is a myth; private options only speed things up for the rich, while the rest face growing queues and crumbling public services. Why assume that the opt-out of affluent patients from the NHS will result in shorter wait times for everyone, when evidence from similar systems shows that public services often face chronic underinvestment as a result? How do you propose to prevent private providers from cherry-picking profitable patients, leaving the NHS to handle the most complex and costly cases? Why do you claim that a mixed healthcare system improves access without sacrificing equity, when evidence from countries like the US shows private involvement often leads to higher costs and unequal outcomes for the poor? This approach ignores how private providers cherry-pick healthy patients, dumping the complex cases back on the NHS and making waits worse for vulnerable people.
